profile.entities: SIS Limited; AP Securitas (APS); SIS International
profile.subseg: India Security; Facility Management; International Security (Aus/NZ); Cash Logistics (Pre-IPO)
profile.themes: Labour Code Implementation; Market Consolidation via Compliance; Margin Recovery to Pre-COVID Levels; Cash Business IPO Deferral

bull_bear.body: Total shareholder return INR 250 cr in FY26 (Dividend + Buyback); Total since IPO ~INR 600 cr. ROCE improved to 16.5% (from 14.3%). Strategy prioritizes 15% ROCE maintenance over aggressive expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in Cash Business IPO due to geopolitical/market volatility; Execution risk in APS integration; Potential lag in customer acceptance of Labour Code rate hikes; Attrition (though managed at ~32% vs industry 42%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; Emphasizes 'inflection point' due to regulatory changes; Clarifies accounting norms on gratuity; Reiterates '15x15' compounding formula; Dismisses cyclical fears highlighting recession-resistant nature of essential services.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Event-driven international revenue (AUD 20m) is recurring annual Q4 phenomenon, not one-off; 60% of new security recruits are graduates (vs 10th pass mandate) to handle digital reporting/apps, yet paid same minimum wage, creating quality arbitrage; Training is subsidized (employees pay INR 7,500), not a cost center.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: India Security: INR 1,925 cr (+34.2% YoY incl. APS), Margin 5.1% (Standalone 5.5%, APS 4.2%); Facility Management: INR 635 cr (+8.1% YoY), Margin 5.5%; International Security: INR 1,950 cr (+36.9% YoY), Margin 3.8% (boosted by Australian Open/Grand Prix).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Labour Codes enforce single license/compliance, eliminating cost arbitrage of unorganized players who previously undercut prices by ignoring statutory dues. | SIS Limited | beneficiary | High | As the largest organized player with full compliance infrastructure, SIS stands to gain significant market share from the fragmentation of non-compliant competitors. Management cites this as a fundamental industry reset. |
| Minimum wage hikes in key states (UP, Haryana) increase cost base for all players, but only organized players have contractual pass-through mechanisms. | SIS Limited | beneficiary | Med | Revenue increases via wage pass-through, but margin expansion depends on speed of client acceptance. Unorganized players may absorb costs or lose contracts. |
| Deferred IPO of Cash business delays value unlocking for shareholders despite strong performance. | SIS Limited | loser | Low | Temporary delay due to external market conditions; DRHP validity extended to Sep 2027. Business fundamentals remain solid. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Consolidated EBITDA margin 4.6%; India Security standalone 5.5%; FM 5.5%; Intl 3.8%. Cost pressure from minimum wage hikes (UP +28%, Haryana +50%) is fully pass-through to clients, actually boosting top-line. Synergy target: Converge APS margin from 4.2% to 5.5% within 1.5 years.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: >15% CAGR multi-year target; Margin: Targeting return to 6% EBITDA (pre-COVID levels) over 12-18 months; Order Inflow: Steady state, no specific new guidance; Capex/Commissioning: Focused on tech integration and branch consolidation post-APS; Cash IPO: Deferred to FY27 pending market stability.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: International contracts typically 3-5 years; Event-based revenue (AUD 20m/INR 120 cr) recurring annually in Q4; India security contracts seeing rate renegotiations due to Labour Codes.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Market share consolidation as Labour Codes enforce compliance (currently <5% share vs 15%+ in mature markets); Cross-selling tech solutions; APS synergy (50 bps margin uplift expected in 12-18 months); Wage inflation pass-through driving nominal revenue growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SIS delivered record Q4FY26 revenue (INR 4,489 cr, +31% YoY) and EBITDA (INR 207 cr, 4.6% margin) driven by APS consolidation and event-driven international spikes, signaling a structural inflection as new Labour Codes neutralize compliance arbitrage for unorganized competitors. While the Cash IPO is deferred to FY27 due to market conditions, the core security/FM platform is compounding at >15% with ROCE now exceeding 16.5%, validating the '15x15' growth-return framework.
